description: We are a team of space-loving storytellers from Egypt who believe science should feel like an adventure. Our project, “Forgotten Explorers,” brings NASA’s Spirit and Opportunity rovers to life for children with a bilingual interactive website, storybook, video, and coloring book. Join us if you love space or creativity! We’re looking for skills in video editing, illustration, animation, web development, or Arabic/English writing.
summary:
We created a storytelling project called “Forgotten Explorers,” which tells the stories of NASA’s two twin rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, which were operating on Mars. These rovers were designed for 90 days of operations, but Opportunity continued to work for approximately 14 years. We have an interactive bilingual (English/Arabic) website with a 10 page storybook you can read to them, a rover-parts explorer to explore, real NASA pictures, a dust-storm game, and a quiz. We also developed a printable storybook, a 10 slide presentation, a 25 second video and coloring book.

The project is designed to work out the challenge and put the dense mission data like water evidence, the first marathon on another planet and the 2018 dust storm as a simple, emotional story for school age children. This does not only represent active missions, but also the silent rovers!

It's significant because it demonstrates how history inspires the next generation on space exploration. The lesson the twins learn is that there is no time like the present to be determined, and that you can have big dreams.
details:
Clear, concise, and informative description of what it does and how it works.

This book, “Forgotten Explorers,” narrates the stories of NASA’s two Mars rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, in different forms for kids. The main part is a bilingual (English/Arabic) website. It features a 10 page storybook which children can flip through, tap to make come to life, and have read to them. It also includes a “Did you know?” fact per page, an explorer of the rover parts that you can click on, a gallery of real images taken by NASA, a dust-covered solar panel power-drop game, a 5 question quiz, and a time line. We created a printable story book, a ten slide presentation, a 25 second video and a coloring book around the site.

Benefits

Children learn complex science in simple terms, their own terms, with pictures, sound and play. These formats are suited to different contexts – classroom, screen, print.

Intended impact

We want children to recognise that there is some history in the old, silent, space machines and we want them to feel curious about Mars and space exploration. The twins' message is that determination never ends and that “big dreams” can come true!

Tools and technologies

All the website was developed in HTML, CSS and JavaScript without using any frameworks. For the read aloud button, it utilises the speech feature built into the browser.

NASA, JPL Mars Exploration Rover pages provided facts and images.

To write and structure the website in code, we utilized the AI assistant Claude, as well as to summarise our research.

Include the tools you employed in the presentation, video and coloring book.

Creativity

We did not treat the rovers as a data sheet, but as characters with a story to tell. The dust game had them feel the problem that the mission ended with, and the storybook, video, coloring book had them engage in different ways.

Factors we considered

Target audience: school-aged children, using simple language, short pages, large illustrations.

Language: Arabic and English - to allow more families to read.

Accuracy: checked with NASA dates and numbers, corrected inconsistencies in own text.

Accessibility: keyboard controls, image text and minimised movement for those sensitive to it.
